text:
Mina: Heads-up: staging linkcheck flagged a few anchor mismatches after the MDX roll. One weird case: we have links that rely on mixed-case headings and the new slugifier lowercased everything so fragments are breaking.

DocsBot: Linkcheck failed on build #511: https://ci.redwood/511 :warning:

Mina: Log excerpt:
```
WARN Broken fragment: /examples/sdk.md#QuickStart -> fragment not found
WARN Broken fragment: /guides/permissions.md#OAuth-Scopes -> fragment not found
```

Eli: Ah, yup. Docusaurus slugify normalizes to lowercase by default, and our previous MkDocs setup preserved case in some generated anchors. So `#QuickStart` became `#quickstart` and `#OAuth-Scopes` became `#oauth-scopes`.

Rae: How many refs are affected? I grepped for `#QuickStart` and `#OAuth-Scopes` across docs/ and examples/ — found 6 occurrences total (two in examples, four in tutorial references).

Sam: Two ways to fix: 1) update all referring links to the new lowercase slugs, or 2) add explicit short ids on the headings to preserve the old mixed-case anchors, e.g. `### QuickStart {#QuickStart}`. I prefer canonicalizing to lowercase links to match docusaurus convention. Less surprising long term.

Eli: Agreed on canonicalizing, but we should be careful with external links (blog posts, external docs) that may rely on old casing. For those, adding an explicit id is safer. We can do a hybrid: update all internal refs to lowercase and add explicit ids on the target headings for backwards compatibility for external links.

Mina: Plan: - Update all internal references to lowercase slugs - Add explicit `{#QuickStart}` and `{#OAuth-Scopes}` ids on the target headings where appropriate - Run linkcheck and add a tiny test that validates fragment targets for changed files only.

DocsBot: Suggested PR checklist:
- [ ] Replace mixed-case fragment links with lowercase variants in examples and tutorials
- [ ] Add explicit heading ids on impacted pages where we know external links exist
- [ ] Run `pnpm docs:build && pnpm docs:linkcheck` locally
- [ ] Add `tests/test_fragments_changed.sh` to CI

Rae: I can patch the six refs and add the heading ids in the same PR. Will also run the site build locally.

Sam: When you add the explicit ids, please use stable, simple ids (no spaces or punctuation) and prefer lowercase too for new ids, but include the legacy mixed-case one if we need to preserve it. Eg: `### QuickStart {#quickstart #QuickStart}` (mdx accepts multiple ids).

Eli: FYI Docusaurus accepts multiple ids but some markdown parsers collapse them; prefer single explicit legacy id if necessary. If we add both, test on staging.

Rae: Noted. I'll use legacy id only for headings that have external backlinks (we can check google analytics or referer logs if needed). For internal links we'll update to lowercase.

Mina: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/921 - updates 6 refs to lowercase, adds explicit legacy ids on targets for external-suspect pages, and includes `tests/check_fragments_changed.sh`.

DocsBot: PR 921 - linkcheck step queued.

Eli: Ran `pnpm docs:linkcheck` locally against the branch; all fragments present. Added a small unit to fail if a changed file references a missing fragment.

DocsBot: CI for PR 921 - linkcheck passed :white_check_mark: Full build green.

Sam: Merged. Staging linkcheck green. Nice and tidy.

Mina: Follow-up: file a short note in docs/migration-notes.md about slug differences and recommend using lowercase fragment links going forward. Also let's add a note in the contributor guide about adding explicit ids for public-facing headings.

Rae: I'll file the infra ticket to add a pre-commit hook that runs the changed-file fragment check script; this would catch it before the PR.

Mina: Thanks everyone. Closing thread. :tada:
